title: Overly Permissive Firebase Storage Read Access
description: The Firebase Storage security rules allowed unauthenticated users to read objects from the /uploads bucket, exposing potentially sensitive user data.
root_cause: The storage.rules file contained an `allow read: if true;` rule which granted global read access without requiring authentication.
intended_behavior: Only authenticated users should be able to read files from the /uploads bucket.

trace.description: Global read access is permitted by `allow read: if true;`.
The overly permissive rule exposes all objects under /uploads/{imageId} to anyone.

conditions.description: An attacker does not need an account or valid session.
An attacker knows or can guess object paths (e.g., /uploads/image123.jpg).

execution.attacker_perspective: As an unauthenticated user, I can send an HTTP GET request to the Firebase Storage endpoint to download any image if I know its name.
instructions: Obtain the Firebase Storage endpoint URL for the target project.
Send an HTTP GET request for an object in the /uploads bucket.
Observe that the object is returned successfully.
execution.observed_result: The server returns a 200 OK status and the contents of the image, despite the lack of authentication.

remediation.strategy: Change the read rule in storage.rules to require authentication by checking `request.auth != null`.

likelihood.reason: Exploitation only requires making a standard HTTP GET request. Object names might be guessable or leaked elsewhere.

impact.reason: Unauthenticated users can access arbitrary uploaded images, violating confidentiality, though they cannot modify or delete them.

confidence.reason: The rule explicitly and unambiguously allows public read access.
